pr_title: samples: net: mqtt: Add a sample to connect to AWS IoT core
pr_body:
I would like to propose the addition of a new sample application to Zephyr RTOS, which implements an MQTT client that can publish messages to AWS IoT Core using the MQTT protocol. The sample showcases the implementation of key features such as establishing a TLS 1.2 connection with AWS IoT Core, subscribing to a topic, and publishing data. Additionally, this sample is designed to pass the test suite for the AWS Device Qualification Program (DQP).

This sample can be used as a starting point for developers who are interested in building their own IoT solutions using Zephyr RTOS and AWS IoT Core.

The sample has been tested on the ST NUCLEO-F429ZI board and QEMU x86. I have taken other net/cloud samples as examples, so there are similarities in parts of the code.

Please let me know if you have any questions, feedbacks or concerns.

Fixes #22866

review_comments:
Files `dhcp.c` and `dhcp.h` were copied from https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/samples/net/cloud/google_iot_mqtt/src/dhcp.c without any modification and I kept the license. I also didn't want to change the style. 

What would you suggest, should I fix code style for the sample only and update the license by adding a line ?
I made the changes and updated the license in `dhcp.h` and `dhcp.c`

Ah, I've started to wonder how does it work if you only provide device certificate tag and no root CA, but now I see they're all regsitered under the same tag number.

I think it'd be a bit more readable, if root CA received its own tag, as it's not related to the device credentials. Device private tag and cert should share the same tag though, as they come in couple.
Fixed, I always thought it was the intended way to do, but now that I have your explanation, I do agree.
I'd also check for POLLHUP and POLLERR here, and break if set.
It's more of a convention, but we aim to define variables at the top of the block.
